slides.0.title: White grape varieties
slides.0.subtitle: Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay and more
slides.1.title: The white-grape picture
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Total area in 2025
slides.1.highlights.0.content: In 2025 vineyards covered about 86,525 ha; white varieties about 55.8% and red about 44.2%
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Chenin Blanc
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The most planted variety: about 15,949 ha in 2025 (about 18.4%); traditionally called Steen locally
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Sauvignon Blanc and Colombard
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Sauvignon Blanc about 12.1% (10,442 ha); Colombard about 10.6% (9,155 ha)
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Chardonnay
slides.1.highlights.3.content: About 7.6% (6,574 ha); also one of the main varieties of Cap Classique
slides.1.content: All figures are for 2025 and change each year; check the latest official numbers for exams.
slides.2.title: The many faces of Chenin Blanc
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Acidity and versatility
slides.2.highlights.0.content: High acidity and clear fruit make it suitable for sparkling, dry, off-dry and sweet wines and distilling stock
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Old vines
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Old-vine Chenin is a highlight of South African whites, covered later in the Swartland and Old Vine Project lessons
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Compare with the Loire
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Chenin Blanc's home is the Loire; South Africa's warmer climate tends to show riper fruit
slides.2.content: Treat Chenin Blanc as South Africa's white lead and compare it with the Loire.
